title: Additive transport for uniformly bounded bicomplex totals
statement: Let $C$ and $D$ be preadditive categories [def-weil-preadditive-category], assume that $C$ has a zero object and finite coproducts, and let $F:C\to D$ be additive [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor]. Let $B$ be an integer-indexed commuting bicomplex in $C$: it consists of objects $B^{p,q}$ and maps $d_1:B^{p,q}\to B^{p+1,q}$ and $d_2:B^{p,q}\to B^{p,q+1}$ satisfying $d_1^2=d_2^2=0$ and $d_1d_2=d_2d_1$. Its diagonal total has terms $\operatorname{Tot}(B)^n=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}B^{p,q}$ and differential induced on the $(p,q)$ summand by $d_1+(-1)^p d_2$. Write $F B$ for the bicomplex obtained by applying $F$ to all objects and differentials. Assume that for some integer $b$, $B^{p,q}$ is a zero object whenever $p>b$ or $q>0$. Then the diagonal coproducts defining $\operatorname{Tot}(B)$ and $\operatorname{Tot}(F B)$ exist, $F$ preserves each diagonal coproduct of $B$, and the canonical `mapTotalIso` isomorphism identifies $\operatorname{Tot}(F B)$ with $F(\operatorname{Tot}(B))$, where $F$ acts termwise on the latter complex. These isomorphisms are natural for bicomplex maps between any two bicomplexes satisfying these bounds, even when their first-index upper bounds differ.

proof.text: Fix a total degree n and let $I_n=\{(p,q):p+q=n\}$. If $B^{p,q}$ with $(p,q)\in I_n$ is not a zero object, the support hypotheses give $p\le b$ and $q\le 0$, hence $n=p+q\le p\le b$. So the set $J_n=\{(p,n-p):n\le p\le b\}$ is finite (empty when $n>b$) and every term of $I_n\setminus J_n$ is a zero object. Since $C$ has finite coproducts, the finite family $(B^{p,q})_{J_n}$ has a coproduct $S$ with injections $\iota_{p,q}$. Put $\iota_{p,q}=0:B^{p,q}\to S$ for $(p,q)\in I_n\setminus J_n$. This is a coproduct of the whole diagonal family: given maps $f_{p,q}:B^{p,q}\to T$ for $(p,q)\in I_n$, the unique $g:S\to T$ with $g\iota_{p,q}=f_{p,q}$ on $J_n$ also satisfies it off $J_n$, because a map out of a zero object is unique, so $f_{p,q}=0=g\circ 0$; uniqueness of $g$ is already forced by $J_n$. Hence the diagonal coproduct defining $\operatorname{Tot}(B)^n$ exists. Additivity gives $F(0)=0$, so $FB$ is a bicomplex, and $F$ sends a zero object $Z$ to a zero object ($\mathrm{id}_{FZ}=F(\mathrm{id}_Z)=F(0)=0$); thus $FB^{p,q}$ is a zero object off $J_n$. By [lem-sfb-left-resolution-additive-finite-coproducts], $(FS,F\iota_{p,q})_{J_n}$ is a coproduct of $(FB^{p,q})_{J_n}$; the same zero-extension argument in $D$ shows that $(FS,F\iota_{p,q})_{I_n}$, whose maps off $J_n$ are $F(0)=0$, is a coproduct of the whole diagonal family of $FB$. So the diagonal coproducts of $\operatorname{Tot}(FB)$ exist and $F$ carries the coproduct cocone of each diagonal of $B$ to a coproduct cocone, i.e. preserves it.

proof.text: With the totals and preservation hypotheses established in Step 1, apply [lem-sfb-left-resolution-map-total-iso] to obtain the componentwise canonical mapTotalIso isomorphism Tot(F B) ≅ F(Tot(B)). The comparison is a chain isomorphism because F maps the two bicomplex differentials and their signed sum, and the source construction checks this on each coproduct injection.

For a bicomplex map φ:B→B′ between any two bicomplexes satisfying the stated support bounds (with no requirement that their chosen upper bounds agree), the naturality equation in [lem-sfb-left-resolution-map-total-iso] identifies Tot(Fφ) followed by the comparison for B′ with the comparison for B followed by F(Tot φ). Therefore the family of mapTotalIso comparisons is natural even when the first-index bounds differ.

lean.statement: theorem additive_total_transport {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] [Preadditive C] [HasZeroObject C] [HasFiniteCoproducts C] {D : Type uD} [Category.{vD} D] [Preadditive D] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive] (B : HomologicalComplex₂ C (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) (b : ℤ) [CochainComplex.IsStrictlyLE B b] [∀ p : ℤ, CochainComplex.IsStrictlyLE (B.X p) 0] : ∃ (hB : B.HasTotal (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) (hP : F.PreservesTotalComplex B (ComplexShape.up ℤ)), IsIso (additiveTotalComparison F B hB hP).hom ∧ ∀ (B' : HomologicalComplex₂ C (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) (b' : ℤ) [CochainComplex.IsStrictlyLE B' b'] [∀ p : ℤ, CochainComplex.IsStrictlyLE (B'.X p) 0] (φ : B ⟶ B'), ∃ (hB' : B'.HasTotal (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) (hP' : F.PreservesTotalComplex B' (ComplexShape.up ℤ)), total.map ((F.mapHomologicalComplex₂ (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map φ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ≫ (additiveTotalComparison F B' hB' hP').hom = (additiveTotalComparison F B hB hP).hom ≫ (F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map (total.map φ (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
lean.note: The helper additiveTotalComparison is the canonical mapTotalIso with explicit total and preservation witnesses.
